label: text

label: text
text: FOR BRIEF

label: text
text: Railway Strikers Return to Work.

label: text
text: PRICE, $3.00 Per Month.

label: text
text: The Prime Minister has submitted to the miners and coal owners a memorandum embodying fresh proposals for ending the crisis in the industry. A National Wages Board will be established, and meanwhile a subsidy of £3,000,000 will be granted by the Government.

label: text
text: The railway strike is over. Negotiations as regards the docks and certain forms of transport are pursuing a normal course.

label: paragraph_title
text: LATEST INFORMATION

label: paragraph_title
text: (Rentor's Service.)

label: text
text: London, May 14.

label: text
text: Mr. S. Baldwin, Prime Minister, was loudly cheered by the Conservatives and to some extent by the Labourites when he gave the House of Commons the latest authoritative information as regards the industrial situation before the separation for the week-end.

label: text
text: He said that the negotiations as regards the docks and certain forms of transport were pursuing a normal course.

label: text
text: An agreement had been reached for the resumption of the bus, trumway, and tube services to-morrow, but the terms of settlement were not yet available.

label: text
text: He next referred to the prospects of an imminent railway agreement which was shortly after entered into.

label: text
text: The Prime Minister, in conclusion, said that there was no possibility of the parties in the mining dispute agreeing between themselves. He therefore had prepared proposals which he was of opinion would form a reasonable and fair basis for the agreement which would be handed to them at the week-end for consideration.

label: text
text:
London, May 14.
Mr. Baldwin's proposals have been submitted to the owners and miners. "He proposes to introduce in the present session a number of Bills embodying the Coal Commission's recommendations, to grant a temporary subsidy of £3,000,000; to establish a joint Board with an independent Chairman to frame wages conditions pending the permanent re-organisation of the industry.

label: text
text:
Comprehensive Legislation.
In Mr. Baldwin's proposals the legislation foreshadowed is most comprehensive. It deals with amalgamations of mines, the establishment of a Coal Advisory Committee, a Nation Wages Board, a National Fuel and Power Council containing representatives of Labour, and a Committee to investigate the question of selling by syndicates.

label: text
text: The proposals require the miners to accept a reduction in the minimum wages other than the subsistence rates for a short undefined period, whilst the owners will bear wages equivalent to 100 per cent. of the net proceeds based on the January—March quarter as far as is necessary to maintain those wages. The Government will all the gap with a subsidy not exceeding £3,000,000.

label: text
text:
National Wages Board.
Meantime a Board will be established consisting of three representatives each of the owners and miners, with an independent Chairman, to frame a national wages and hours agreement and to decide the principle on which district rates can be ascertained.

label: text
text: The Board shall issue a decision within three weeks.

label: text
text: Finally the proposals stipulate that the provisional undertakings by the Government are conditional on the acceptance of the terms of the memorandum by all parties.

label: paragraph_title
text: RIGHT CONCLUSION.

label: text
text: (British Wireless Service.)

label: text
text:
Rugby, May 14.
Mr. Ramsay MacDonald, the Labour leader, expressed his satisfaction at the Prime Minister's statement. He added that he was certain that the Prime Minister had come to the right conclusion in regard to the mines difficulty, and he was very glad that Mr. Baldwin had taken the step of making his own proposals.
General Return to Work.
In regard to other industries which were concerned in the strike reports from various parts of the country tell of the general return of the men to work to-day. In spite of the difficulty over the reinstatement of dockers, the Board of Trade announces that the dockers at Liverpool resumed work this morning in good numbers at the old wages and hours.

label: text
text:
Some Normal Industries.
The general strike has, of course, caused a considerable amount of dislocation in most industries which were not directly affected by it. But many industries have been able throughout the strike to maintain nearly normal production. Among these may be mentioned those of motor and other cycles, carpets, soaps, and surgical instruments. A number of paper mills working for export have continued to produce. Even in the iron and steel industry some blast furnaces in Scotland and the Midlands have been working throughout the strike at full pressure.

label: paragraph_title
text: RAILWAY STRIKE OVER

label: text
text:
The railway strike is settled.
Terms of Settlement:

label: text
text: The terms of the agreement between the Railway Companies and the Unions provide that strikers will be taken back as traffic offers and work can be found. The principle to be followed in reinstatement will be seniority in each grade.

label: text
text: The Trade Unions admit that in calling the strike they committed a wrongful act against the Companies and agree that the Companies do not by re-instatement surrender their legal rights to claim damages arising out of the strike from the strikers and others responsible.

label: text
text: The Unions undertake, firstly, not again to call a strike without previous negotiations; secondly, to give no support of any kind to their members to take unauthorised action; and, thirdly, not to encourage supervisory employees to participate in any strike.

label: text
text: The Companies Intimate that it may be necessary arising out of the strike, to remove certain persons to other positions, but without a reduction in wages.

label: text
text: Each Company will notify the Unions within a week of the names of the men it is proposed to transfer and will afford each mah an opportunity of having an advocate to present his case to the General Manager.

label: text
text: The settlement does not apply to persons guilty of violence and intimidation.

label: text
text: The Trades Union Congress reports considerable improvement in the situation between workers and employers. It declares that firms and big companies are more inclined to meet representatives of the workmen and make arrangements for the resumption of work without raising the question of new agreements.

label: text
text: There is still no settlement of the printing strike.

label: text
text: A conference in London between the Master Printer's Newspapers Society and the Printing Trade. Unions discussed the restarting of the general printing trade in London and the provinces for ten hours to-day, but adjourned. Similarly a further meeting between the Newspaper Proprietors' Association, representing the London newspapers, and the Printing Unions proved abortive and was adjourned.

label: paragraph_title
text: CANTON CRISIS

label: text
text: STILL "MARKING TIME:"

label: text
text: Last night a rumour was currently locally that a Chinese banker had received a telegram indicating that fighting had broken out in or near Canton. No such intelligence has reached the Naval authorities, and in the event of hostilities, it is practically certain that a wireless report would have been sent down.

label: text
text:
From other reliable sources it is learned that there is little possibility of the humour being correct. The latest information is that a state of tension still exists but it is confidently felt that the rabble of Communism will not dare to pit themselves against the army of General Chang Kai-shek.
Further steps to preserve law and order are reported, such as the garrisoning of the Canton-Kowloon (Chinese section) and Canton-Shikwan Railways.

label: text
text: It is, however, a fact that some local Chinese merchants have received instructions from Canton connections not to ship cargo, either by boat or junk for the present, till the situation is clearer.

label: text
text: The Marion Barclay (Presbyterian) Hospital here has re-opened but another closure is contemplated because of persecution by anti-foreign agitators.

label: paragraph_title
text: HONGKONG BOAT NEAR MACAO

label: text
text: BACK AFTER A MONTH.

label: text
text: After an interval of a month, the story of how a Hongkong trading junk was pirated in waters near Macao has been related.

label: text
text: On April 7, the boat left, with a cargo of kerosene and cowhides for Tam Chow, in the Heungshan district (adjoining Macao).

label: text
text: Two days later the junk was off Lim Leung-Mut. A sampan with eight men on board, brandishing rifles, and revolvers, ordered the junk to stop. They crossed over after the sails had been lowered, drove the crew into the forehold and put down the hatch covers. The boat was then anchored and the pirates collected loot to the value of $540 and rowed off. It took them 45 minutes to make up their bag.

label: text
text: The junk has since returned here and the Water Police have been notified.
